content: To estimate the total number of contraceptive methods used in the previous year, calculate the percentage usage of each contraceptive category. If national or facility-specific targets are unavailable, estimate targets based on the percentage of current use from the previous year and the desired percentage change in usage for each method, such as a 5–10% increase. The number of women who had intrauterine devices (IUDs) or implants inserted should be recorded using the Health Management Information System (HMIS). This data should include both fixed-site and outreach records if they are counted in HMIS reports. Facility or clinic managers should identify all staff working in outpatient clinics focused on infant and child health care. Staff should be listed by title and category, ensuring only currently active staff are included. Include new and trainee staff if they are actively working. Training received in the past five years should be documented, and if a staff member has received the same type of training multiple times, it should only be counted once. Summarize findings by recording the total number of staff and the proportion trained by topic, as well as by category (e.g., doctor, medical assistant, nurse/midwife). To improve family planning services, consolidate findings from Checklists 1–7 and review them with facility staff to identify strengths and areas for improvement. After discussion, agree on the two or three most critical areas for improvement to address within the next three months. For each area, identify the underlying reasons for gaps and propose actions to address them, assigning responsibility and timelines. Debrief with the facility director and staff to finalize and agree on the findings and action plan. Keep a copy of the Facility Priority Actions with the facility director and staff, and decide on a review schedule and responsible parties. When synthesizing findings from multiple facilities, evaluation teams should summarize data from Checklists 1–7 on flip-chart paper and post them on the wall. Data should be recorded for each facility, and if there are more than 18 facilities, additional columns should be added. Summarize data for specific checklists, such as medicines and supplies (Checklist 3), contraceptive usage and targets (Checklist 5), and the total number of women to be reached with modern methods in the next year. Combine data for all facilities and calculate totals for each main facility category (e.g., national hospitals, referral hospitals, and first-level health facilities). Discuss indicators, marking low-performing ones with a red marker and those showing progress with a green marker. Participants should review each checklist summary sheet to identify strengths and priority areas for improvement, reaching consensus on the main findings. To develop an annual implementation plan for improving family planning, review checklist summary tables and monitoring and evaluation data. Identify technical issues or gaps and their underlying causes. Record these areas under relevant program categories. Review actions from the previous annual plan and determine whether they need to continue or if new actions are required. Base priority actions on the underlying reasons for gaps, considering their importance, feasibility with existing resources, and whether they can be initiated within three months. Document agreed-upon priority actions and timelines.
